To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
alloxan diabetes causes a loss of priming effects of acute exposure to glucose on A and, to a greater extent, D cell secretion in the perfusion pancreas of the rat.

(1) glucose fails to induce a priming effect on glucagon secretion, but not on somatostain secretion in perfused rat pancreases from alaxan-diabetic rats, (2) insulin treatment in vivo restores the priming effect of glucagon secretion in alloxan-diabetis rats and (3) alloxan diabetes may exert a cytotoxic effect on the D cell of the rat pancreas.

1) short-term alloxon diabetes leads to a loss of a priminig effect of glucose on pancreatic A cell secretion; 2) the abnormality is secondary, at least in part, to insulinopenia; and 3) alloxan diabetes also leads to a loss in the ability of glucose to stimulate pancreatic D cell secretion, and this abnormality persists even when diabetes is treated with exogenous insulin.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of diabetes on glucose regulation of pancreatic A and D cell secretory responsiveness in vivo.
the effects of diabetes on the regulation of pancreatic A and D cell secretory function.
the effects of alloxan diabetes on the secretion of glucagon and somatostatin in the perfused rat pancreas.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
alloxan-induced diabetes in rats leads to loss of priming effects of acute glucose on glucagon and somatostatin release.
alloxan diabetes, at least in the rat, leads to loss of the normal priming effect of a high glucose level on glucagon secretion but not on somatostain secretion.
alloxan diabetes causes a loss of a primine effect of glucose on pancreatic glucagon and somatostatin release.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

alloxan-induced diabetes leads to a loss of a glucagon priming effect of 27.8 mmol/l glucose, which is restored by insulin treatment in vivo, but that the loss of a somatostatin priming effect of the same concentration of glucose is not corrected by insulin treatment.

alloxan-induced insulinopenia and alloxan per se have different effects on the pancreatic islets and that the latter is the major cause for the loss of glucose priming effect on glucagon and somatostatin release.
the glucose priming effect on glucagon release is insulin dependent, whereas the glucose priming effects on somatostain release are independent of the presence of insulin.
The main takeaway from our work is that

alloxan diabetes, in rats at least, causes a loss of priming effects of acute glucose on A and B cell secretion, and that the effect of insulin on glucagon secretion may be mediated through its effect on the priming action of glucose.
the priming effects of the A and D cells are not the same.
the priming effect is not a general phenomenon in all cell types.
